Sim is a strict superset of real's grid; round 5's +0.00 was measured without a domain map. lam 0.3 and 1.0 tie. arm: capacity x regularization (w48/w96 x dropout, 400 ep)
instrument: AoA 15-20 proxy + full split + gap.py, one seed each
effect: BOARD +0.166 (T2R2 80.853 -> T2R3 81.019, NEW BEST): sps +1.013, tke -2.90 % of error, rel_l2 +0.64 % (worse), mvpe +2.49 % (worse), time -1.124 (1.41 board ms). 3-vs-3 first: proxy wfinal 78.466 -> 78.630, full split 80.865 -> 81.124
note: The mechanism is the point. In-sample rho climbs 0.634 -> 0.863 with capacity, so the underfitting IS fixed and nearly all the new fit goes to memorization (seen/unseen gap 1.10x -> 1.75x) -- round 8's reading of its own ladder was right. What is new: held-out rho moves for the first time (0.609 -> 0.620), it moves WITH the regularizer not against it, and the gain sits almost entirely in sps (+0.92), i.e. the error tail. Dropout is monotone through 0.30 and not exhausted. Since the gain looks variance-driven and ensembling already reduces variance, the 1.15 test is the one that decides it -- this is exactly how ozdo died. | SHIPPED as T2R3 (8 all-data w96, 4x do30 + 4x do45, 400 ep, fp16) after passing the 1.15 ensemble test 3-vs-3. The BOARD reading is sharper than the local one: the entire gain arrived through SPS and TKE while rel_l2 went the WRONG way, i.e. capacity+dropout removes per-element TAIL, not rms -- exactly the 'tail reduction beats mean reduction' corollary of SPS's containment scoring, and the first arm to demonstrate it on the board. The local accuracy delta was -1.2 % of error, BELOW the ~4 % transfer resolution, so the transfer is better than the instrument could resolve. Still missing: the interior Re-band k-fold confirmation (Q4).
